prompt: A data set has a minimum of $12$ and a range of $37$. What is the maximum value in the data set?
hint: Recall how the range of a data set is defined. It links the two extreme values by one subtraction.

hints.text: Recall how the range of a data set is defined. It links the two extreme values by one subtraction.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try small numbers: a set with minimum $5$ and range $10$ has maximum $15$, since $15 - 5 = 10$. Range is max minus min, so max is min plus range.
Range equals maximum minus minimum, so the maximum equals the minimum plus the range. Here that is $12 + 37$.
Since $12 + 37 = 49$, the maximum value in the data set is $49$.

learningObjective: Rearrange the definition of range to find a missing extreme.
explanation: The range is the maximum minus the minimum, so the maximum equals the minimum plus the range.
Add the given numbers to find the maximum: $12 + 37 = 49$.
Check with the definition: $49 - 12 = 37$, so the maximum value is $49$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Range says nothing about the middle
steps: Two data sets can share a range of $37$ and look nothing alike — one clustered, one evenly spread.
Range uses only the two extreme values, which also makes it very sensitive to outliers.
That is why the SAT pairs range questions with standard deviation questions: they measure spread in genuinely different ways.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Subtracting the given numbers — 37 − 12 = 25 — misreads which quantity is which.
Range = max − min, so max = min + range. Rearrange the definition BEFORE substituting and the two numbers cannot collide.
